steps.what: Interview patients about symptoms and health histories while clarifying uncertainty and relevant context
Document symptoms and history in a draft encounter note

loop.purpose: Draft a history note from the actual interview without adding diagnoses.
loop.input: Authorised encounter capture and confirmed encounter identity.
loop.output: Draft distinguishing reported symptoms, history, negations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Practitioner checks identity, attribution, dates, medication statements, negations and missing symptoms against the actual interview, correcting unsupported content.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unclear capture or restricted recording returns to manual note entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Try native note templates first; varied patient narratives require language interpretation.

steps.what: Check the history note and accept the exact corrected record version

tasks.design: Use native templates in the patient record system {OTHER}, then bounded note drafting where authorised interview capture is available. The practitioner retains the full interview and checks the exact note before acceptance; the system makes no diagnostic decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative symptoms had to be translated into a record after clarification with the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Consultation note drafting can assist documentation while keeping practitioner validation.
tasks.still_hard: Omitted negations or confused attribution can alter the clinical meaning.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner asks follow-up questions and checks what the patient actually meant.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less note composition; interview effort and clinical responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Distinguish patient reports from confirmed findings and communicate unresolved concerns.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation notes for clinician validation; that capability does not establish diagnosis or this practitioner's legal scope.
The proposed task savings are model knowledge and are not inferred from vendor minutes-per-consult claims.

assumptions: Boundary covers interview and history documentation; diagnosis and referral work are separately scoped. The occupational title does not establish medical registration or authority.

During s1 practitioner confirms patient/encounter IDs and permission and sets up permitted audio or dictated capture of the clarified account. Capture setup and clarification are counted. In s2 the permitted service produces draft text from that capture; no pre-existing transcript or structured symptoms are assumed, and unavailable capture returns to manual entry.
OTHER means patient record system. Native templates precede note drafting; health-data access and recording conditions must be confirmed for the actual practice.
research_questions: Does comparison with the actual interview expose negation, attribution and omission errors before acceptance?

incremental.description: Review note quality samples and update templates.
Records administrator maintains permitted access and capture configuration.

approvals.approved_version: Exact corrected note, encounter identity and source capture reference; edits void acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=93 gross=7 net=3 after 4 upkeep. Zero if recording is unavailable or correction exceeds manual entry; 1 for a clear narrative with unchanged interview time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess health conditions within authorised scope

steps.what: Assess symptoms, histories and test results to diagnose conditions or seek qualified clinical assessment

tasks.design: Keep clinical assessment with an appropriately qualified human using the patient record system {OTHER}. Where the practitioner lacks diagnostic authority or competence, seek qualified clinical assessment; this proposal adds no diagnostic model.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagnosis depends on clinical context, uncertainty and appropriate professional competence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support assessment without establishing autonomous diagnostic capability.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete histories and nonspecific results can obscure serious conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The human recognises uncertainty and the need for prompt qualified assessment.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in clinical judgement or extension of scope.

reach.learn: Communicate observed findings and uncertainty without unsupported diagnostic claims.

evidence.claim: Retaining clinical diagnosis with appropriately qualified professionals is model knowledge; generic record tools do not establish diagnostic competence.

assumptions: Boundary is assessment, excluding separately scoped interviewing, test ordering and referral execution.
Practitioner reviews actual history and results in s1; no structured diagnosis, urgency or reassuring-result flag is assumed.
OTHER is patient record system. Existing native record access is considered first. Zero upkeep because no new workflow is introduced; actual national scope and registration are unknown.
research_questions: Which assessment findings require immediate qualified clinical evaluation under the practice's actual escalation arrangements?

already_counted.description: All assessment and scope judgement remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Clinical judgement remains fully human and no new authority is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult health professionals and refer patients

steps.what: Consult other health professionals about patient care and the need for referral
Check referral details and communicate the referral or request for qualified clinical assessment

tasks.design: Retain professional consultation through {TELEPHONY} and checked referral communication through the patient record system {OTHER}. The practitioner acts within actual scope and confirms the destination, information and escalation arrangements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination depends on clinical uncertainty and the receiving professional's role.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication tools support referrals without removing clinical discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Sending a request does not establish that appropriate care has been received.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner communicates uncertainty and recognises when further escalation is needed.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in consultation or referral effort.

reach.learn: Provide clear reasons, relevant findings and unresolved questions.

evidence.claim: Professional consultation and referral judgement remain human work, based on model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is focal consultation and referral communication; receiving clinicians' assessment remains outside and unchanged.
Practitioner produces consultation findings during s1 and verifies identity, recipient and permitted disclosure in retained s2; no free referral suitability or acceptance flag is assumed.

OTHER means patient record system. Native referral tools are considered first. Zero upkeep because no new drafting or routing workflow is introduced; authority remains subject to actual national rules.
research_questions: How does the actual practice confirm that a patient needing qualified assessment reaches the appropriate service?

already_counted.description: All consultation, referral checking and communication remain counted.

incremental.description: No new upkeep or transferred work introduced.

approvals.approved_version: Exact recipient, patient identity, referral text and disclosed records; changes require renewed checking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Consultation and checked referral work remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Request imaging or arrange qualified referral

steps.what: Assess the need for diagnostic imaging and determine the authorised ordering or referral route
Check imaging request details and submit an authorised order or qualified referral request
outputs: authorised imaging order or referral request

tasks.design: Keep imaging indication and route selection with a qualified human using the patient record system {OTHER}. If this practitioner cannot order the procedure, communicate a request for qualified assessment rather than treating the occupation title as ordering authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Indication, suitability and authority require individual assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing order or referral tools support communication without replacing professional decisions.
tasks.still_hard: The appropriate procedure and route depend on clinical context and actual scope.
tasks.human_edge: The human recognises limitations and ensures the request reaches a qualified decision-maker.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in imaging decisions or increase in authority.

reach.learn: Communicate the clinical question and relevant limitations.

evidence.claim: Retaining imaging indication and authorised ordering decisions is model knowledge; no applicable autonomous ordering capability is established.

assumptions: Boundary is imaging-specific route selection and checked request, excluding general referrals counted elsewhere and procedure execution.
Practitioner determines actual route and authority in s1, then checks identity, procedure, clinical question and recipient in s2. No pre-existing suitability or ordering-authority flag is assumed.
OTHER means patient record system. Consider native forms first. Zero upkeep because no new automated workflow is introduced; national scope and qualifications need confirmation.
research_questions: Which imaging requests require assessment by a different authorised clinician before an order can exist?

already_counted.description: All route judgement and checked request communication remain counted.

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, imaging request or referral, clinical question and recipient; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Imaging decisions and authorised communication remain human without an assumed scope extension.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: History-note drafting may reduce a small amount of composition while interviewing, clinical assessment and referral decisions remain human.
reach: Coordinate unresolved concerns with qualified clinicians under the practice's actual scope.
role.ambitious_version: A practitioner who maintains accurate histories and promptly involves qualified clinicians where the patient's needs exceed actual competence or authority.
